title: Paramārthasāra
text:
**1**
Supreme, beyond the supreme {{prakṛti / mūlaprakṛti|primal material nature, source of the manifest}}, beginningless, one, [yet] lodged manifoldly in the hidden chambers [of beings], the abode of all, present in all that moves and is unmoving — to you alone, Viṣṇu, do I go for refuge.
**2**
Though the whole world is plunged into the ocean that is the {{ātman / paramātman|the Self / the supreme Self, identified with Viṣṇu}}, it neither sips [of it] nor sees [it]. This is the marvel — that it delights, wholly in vain, in the ocean of becoming, which is [unreal] like a mirage.
**3**
Beholding the world sunk in the ocean of dwelling in the womb-chamber, of coming-to-be, birth, old age, death, and separation [from loved ones], the disciple, with hands folded, spoke to his teacher.
**4**
"You are the knower of the Veda together with its auxiliaries, the shatterer of the host of doubts, the speaker of truth. I ask, O Blessed One, the question of crossing the ocean of {{mokṣa|release, here defined as cutting the knot of ignorance}}-bound transmigration (saṃsāra).
**5**
In this long round of transmigration, whose is the bondage, and through what? Who is it that, by [endless] goings and comings here, experiences {{karma|action and its ripening fruit}} that yields fruit good and ill?
**6**
Bound in the net of action and the {{guṇa|the three constituent qualities of prakṛti}}s, the living self (jīva) transmigrates like the silk-worm [spinning its own cocoon]. From that bondage — a dense thicket of the darkness of delusion — how is its release ({{mokṣa|release, the cutting of the knot of ignorance}}) [to come]?
**7**
'For one who knows the distinction between the {{guṇa|the three qualities of nature}}s and the {{puruṣa|the conscious principle, contrasted with prakṛti}}, merit and demerit are not binding' — by such words [of the tradition] declared before, tell me, [then,] of {{prakṛti / mūlaprakṛti|primal nature}} and {{puruṣa|the conscious self}}."
**8**
Thus questioned by the disciple, the Blessed One, the [world's] support, said to him: "What is to be told here is too deep even for the learned; nevertheless, hear it, you.
**9**
Bowing to that Upendra [Viṣṇu] by whom this world — unreal yet seeming real — was fashioned out of {{prakṛti / mūlaprakṛti|the primal root-nature}}, I shall declare this Essence of Supreme Truth ({{paramārtha|supreme/ultimate reality, as against vyavahāra, the conventional}}sāra)."
**10**
From the unmanifest (avyakta) the [cosmic] egg arose; from the egg, Brahmā; thence the emission of creatures. This whole unfolding, made of {{māyā|the deluding creative power that produces the dual world}}, is in turn withdrawn again, step by step.
**11**
The aggregate of instruments [made] of the {{guṇa|the three qualities}}s, though composed of {{māyā|deluding creative power}} and insentient, performs actions; the embodied one (dehin) that presides over it, though sentient, does nothing whatever.
**12**
Just as iron, though it is insentient, moves when a magnet stands near, so the assemblage of instruments stirs into activity when the body is presided over by consciousness (cit).
**13**
Just as, when the sun has risen, this world of living beings performs its actions, yet the sun neither does those actions nor causes them to be done — so too the {{ātman / paramātman|the Self}}.
**14**
For the deluded mind, swooned [into identity] by the I-sense (ahaṃkāra) and [yet] awakened by consciousness, there arises here the conceit 'I am the person ({{puruṣa|the conscious self}})' and the experiencing of pleasure and pain.

title: Paramārthasāra
text:
**15**
"I am the doer, the enjoyer, the witness of actions high and low" — thus does the {{ātman / paramātman|Self}}, [though] by its own nature stainless and all-pervading, [falsely] presume.
**16**
As a flawless crystal takes on the color of variously colored [objects placed near it], so the all-pervading [Self] takes on the character of the {{upādhi|limiting adjunct that makes the Self appear conditioned}}, which is itself shaped by the {{guṇa|qualities}}s.
**17**
As the sun's reflected disc moves when the water moves and comes to rest when [the water] is still, so here too the {{ātman / paramātman|Self}} [seems to] move when the inner organ (antaḥkaraṇa) moves.
**18**
As Rāhu, though [himself] invisible, becomes manifest to the world when [he] stands upon the disc of the moon, so the {{ātman / paramātman|Self}}, though all-pervading, comes into view when [reflected as] resident in the intellect (buddhi).
**19**
All-pervading, beyond compare, non-dual ({{advaita|non-duality}}) — that is to be reached by the mind; the {{brahman|the absolute, the non-dual ground of being}} which, [reflected as] residing in the intellect, is apprehended — that, O disciple, is what is to be understood.
**20**
Intellect, mind, and I-sense, the subtle elements (tanmātras) and the host of sense-faculties, and the aggregate of gross elements (bhūtas) — these, [products] of {{prakṛti / mūlaprakṛti|nature}}, competent only to bring forth and sustain the round of transmigration, are to be abandoned.
**21**
Merit and demerit, the constructs of pleasure and pain, dwelling in heaven and hell, birth and death, the [four] castes and life-stages — these do not exist here, in {{paramārtha|supreme reality}}.
**22**
Water in a mirage, silver in mother-of-pearl, a serpent on a rope — like the double-moon [seen] by one with diseased sight, the entire form of the world is an error ({{adhyāsa / bhrānti|superimposition / illusory error, as a snake on a rope}}).
**23**
Just as the one sun shines [reflected] in all reservoirs of water, so the {{ātman / paramātman|supreme Self}}, abiding in all the limiting adjuncts ({{upādhi|limiting adjuncts}}s), shines [as many].
**24**
Like space [present] within and without pots and the like, {{brahman|the absolute}} abides in all bodily lumps. The notion 'I' with respect to the body, which is not the Self, makes for the bondage of transmigration.
**25**
Free of all conceptual construction, pure, awakened, ageless and deathless, at peace, stainless, shining once for all, conscious — such is the {{ātman / paramātman|Self}}, all-pervading like space.
**26**
As juice, molasses, sugar-grains, jaggery, and candy are [but] transformations of sugarcane, so the differences of states, many in form, are [transformations] in the {{ātman / paramātman|supreme Self}} alone.
**27**
Discriminative knowing (vijñāna), the Inner Controller (antaryāmin), the vital breath (prāṇa), the Cosmic Person (virāj), the body, [the level of] genus, and finally the [individual] lump — these conventional designations (vyavahāra) regarding that Self are but particular states [of it].
**28**
There is no serpent on the rope — by what cause, then, arises the fear of a snake? Just so, the error of constructing duality is {{avidyā|nescience, the root of the rope-snake error}}; this [dual world] is not real.
**29**
This is that [great] darkness: that, through error, there is Selfhood [imputed] to the non-Self. Deluded men do not know Vāsudeva, the Self of all.
**30**
Spreading himself out, like a net, through the endless distinctions beginning with the vital breath, Vāsudeva [then] withdraws [it again] by his own power, as though at play.

title: Paramārthasāra
text:
**31**
By just those three — Viśva, Taijasa, and Prājña, called the first, the middle, and the last, [namely] waking, dream, and deep sleep, which are [all] of the nature of error — the {{turīya|the fourth, transcending the three states}} is veiled.
**32**
The God, as it were, deludes himself by his own {{māyā|deluding power}} in the form of duality; thus he [also] himself apprehends the Person ({{puruṣa|the conscious self}}), the Self, hidden in the cave [of the heart].
**33**
As, from a fire, by the risings of smoke, manifold shapes appear in the sky, so in Viṣṇu the creation, spread out as duality, appears by his own {{māyā|deluding creative power}}.
**34**
When the mind is calm [the Lord seems] as if calm, when it is glad as if glad, when it is deluded as if deluded; [but this is] only at the level of convention (vyavahāra) — the Lord is not so in {{paramārtha|supreme reality}}.
**35**
As the vault of the sky is not [really] soiled by [passing] clouds or by risings of smoke, so the supreme {{puruṣa|conscious self}} is untouched by the modifications of {{prakṛti / mūlaprakṛti|nature}}.
**36**
And [just as], although a single pot is covered with the grime of smoke and the like, the remaining [pots] do not [thereby] become defiled, so too here is the living self (jīva). [Note: 'eksaminn' is a scribal corruption for 'ekasminn'; the sense is 'although in a single pot'.]
**37**
The {{guṇa|qualities of nature}}s, fixed in the body and senses, perform action for the sake of their own enjoyment. For one who knows 'I am not the doer, nothing is mine,' action does not bind at all.
**38**
The {{karma|action and its ripening}} done by another (i.e. prior) body, by which this [present] body has come into being, must necessarily be enjoyed [to the end]; its extinction is declared [to come] only through [its] being enjoyed.
**39**
Whatever {{karma|accumulated action}} was heaped up before the arising of {{jñāna|liberating knowledge}}, [once] licked by the flame-tongue of the fire of knowledge, becomes — like a seed scorched by fire — no longer capable of [producing] birth.
**40**
And as for whatever action is performed after the arising of knowledge — that too, indeed, does not cling to the doer, as water does not [cling to] a lotus-leaf.
**41**
'The mass of action here is performed by [the instruments of] speech, body, and mind' — so the awakened (buddha) declare. [Therefore:] '[Being] one alone, I am not the doer of these, I am not [the author] of their actions.'
**42**
From the destruction of the seed which is the fruit of action follows the destruction of birth — herein is no doubt. Having awakened thus, [the knower,] his darkness gone, shines, his nature being light, like the sun.
**43**
Just as a tuft of reed-down, blown up by the wind, scatters to the ten directions, so, through the knowledge of the truth concerning {{brahman|the absolute}}, do the [accumulated] actions of the knower of truth [scatter and vanish].
**44**
As clarified butter drawn out of milk, [even when] thrown back into it, does not [recombine] as before, so the conscious {{ātman / paramātman|Self}}, [once] separated from the {{guṇa|qualities}}s of {{prakṛti / mūlaprakṛti|nature}}, does not [revert to them].
**45**
Having dispelled the thicket of {{māyā|deluding power}} composed of the {{guṇa|qualities}}s, as the thousand-rayed [sun dispels] darkness, the {{puruṣa|conscious self}}, ranging within and without, becomes [homogeneous] like a solid block of rock-salt.
**46**
As the body and its limbs are clay alone — [merely] things born of clay's transformation — so the [whole world of] stationary and moving [beings], [though] non-dual ({{advaita|non-duality}}), appears as if dual.

title: Paramārthasāra
text:
**47**
From the one {{kṣetrajña|the field-knower, the embodied conscious self}} the many classes of field-knowers are born, as from a fire that has entered iron [come] showers of sparks on every side.
**48**
They, through the fault of association with the {{guṇa|qualities}}s, [are] as it were bound — like grains of corn by their own husks — and obtain [repeated] birth, so long as they are not burnt by the fire of {{jñāna|knowledge}}.
**49**
The three-stranded {{avidyā|nescience}} produces creation upon the consciousness-natured Self, which is all-pervading, [ever] established, the support of all; [yet] the {{ātman / paramātman|Self}} is nowhere touched by it.
**50**
As, in the case of the serpent [imagined] on a rope, there is no [real] cause and no [real] arising or perishing [of it], so here there is neither origination nor destruction of the world, nor any [real] cause [of it].
**51**
Eternally free of [all] connection with birth, destruction, going, coming, and defilement, the Self of all is, like space [present] in pots and the like, ever conjoined [with all things, yet untouched].
**52**
It is the limiting adjuncts ({{upādhi|limiting adjuncts}}s) that have the conjunction with the good and ill fruits of action, with pleasure and pain. Bondage [arises] from association with these — as [an innocent man is bound] through consorting with thieves, though he is no thief.
**53**
So long as the {{puruṣa|conscious self}} here has [the sense of its own] being, through association with the body, the {{guṇa|qualities}}s, the instruments, and their objects, just so long does it appear as if bound in transmigration by the nooses of {{māyā|deluding power}}.
**54**
Utterly bewildered by [the divisions of] mother, father, son, kinsfolk, wealth, enjoyment, and [their] partition, the creature is whirled about as if on a wheel made of birth, old age, and death.
**55**
Those deluded ones who here worship the {{avidyā|nescience}} fashioned by worldly convention — they, having the nature of [endless] birth and death, come to blind darkness and suffer. [Note: 'lokavyvahāra-' is a scribal corruption for 'lokavyavahāra-'.]
**56**
As frost, foam, and bubbles [are natural] to water, and as smoke [is natural] to fire, so this {{māyā|deluding creative power}} is declared to be of the very nature of Viṣṇu.
**57**
Thus, casting off {{māyā|deluding power}} — [the source of] the construction of duality, error-natured, bewildering — one should contemplatively realize (bhāvayet) the non-dual ({{advaita|non-duality}}) {{brahman|the absolute}}, which is [both] with parts and partless.
**58**
As water [merges] into water, milk into milk, breeze into wind, so, by contemplation (bhāvanā), one attains to becoming-of-the-same-substance with the stainless {{brahman|the absolute}}. [Note: 'kṣiraṃ' is a scribal corruption for 'kṣīraṃ' (milk).]
**59**
When, the whole mass of duality having thus [dissolved] by contemplation, one has attained the state of {{brahman|the absolute}} — for one who beholds everything as {{brahman|the absolute}}, what delusion is there, what grief?
**60**
As a crystal, its limiting adjunct ({{upādhi|limiting adjunct}}) removed, shines stainless by its own radiance, so the lamp of consciousness (cit), free of [all] {{upādhi|limiting adjuncts}}, shines here by its own radiance.
**61**
Untouched by the host of {{guṇa|qualities}}s, the instruments, the body, the vital breaths, the subtle elements, [the level of] genus, and pleasure and pain — this [Self], all-pervading, of the nature of consciousness, is ever stainless.

title: Paramārthasāra
text:
**62**
Seer, hearer, smeller, toucher, taster, and grasper [though it be called], the embodied one (dehin) [is in truth] devoid of body, senses, and intellect; that [Self] is not the doer.
**63**
"I am one, [yet] not established in [only] one place; through the power of [my] sovereignty (aiśvarya) I am spread, like space, throughout this entire [universe]" — herein there is no doubt whatever.
**64**
The very moment one realizes by contemplation 'all this — partless and with parts — is the {{ātman / paramātman|Self}} alone,' that very moment, freed from the thicket of delusion, one has become the supreme Lordly [reality].
**65**
Whatever the passion-blinded proclaim in [their various] established doctrines (siddhānta), scriptures, and reasonings — all of that we approve, [holding it] in the understanding of the doctrine that all is the Self (sarvātmavāda).
**66**
The Blessed One, who has all forms, by whatever disposition (bhāva) he is worshipped, becoming that very disposition, [like a] wish-fulfilling jewel (cintāmaṇi), [duly] grants [the goal].
**67**
Having known the {{ātman / paramātman|Self}} as Nārāyaṇa, the cause of creation, maintenance, and dissolution, one becomes all-knowing, all-pervading, [becomes] the All, the Lord of all.
**68**
The knower of the Self crosses beyond grief; therefore the wise one fears nothing from any quarter. For him there is not even the fear of death from death itself — whence, then, any other [fear]?
**69**
Eternally free of decrease and increase, of the slain and the slayer, of bondage and release — this is the truth of {{paramārtha|supreme reality}}. Whatever is other than this is all untrue.
**70**
Having thus discerned {{prakṛti / mūlaprakṛti|nature}} and the {{puruṣa|conscious self}}, [the sage,] with the net of [conceptual] construction cast off, delighting in the Self, established in [perfect] quietude, becomes the Alone (kevalin — see {{kaivalya / kevalin|absolute aloneness; the liberated one}}).
**71**
As the reed, the plantain, the bamboo, and the [hollow] cane perish once they have come to their own flowering, so [the upādhis,] become [merely] one's [transient] nature, perish on attaining [their fulfilled] nature.
**72**
When the knot of ignorance is split, when the host of doubts is cut through, when [the store of] merit is exhausted and the seed of birth is burnt up, one goes to the supreme Self, Hari.
**73**
{{mokṣa|release, redefined here non-spatially}} has no abode whatever, nor any going-away to some other place. The splitting of the knot [woven] of ignorance — that they know as release (mokṣa).
**74**
Having awakened thus [to the fact] that this form of the world, made of Viṣṇu's {{māyā|deluding power}}, is unreal, one should become tranquil, free of the pairs of opposites, of limiting adjuncts ({{upādhi|limiting adjuncts}}s), and of attachment to enjoyment.
**75**
Having understood {{prakṛti / mūlaprakṛti|nature}} as [a thing] apart [from himself], the {{puruṣa|conscious self}}, [though] moving in the midst of transmigration, becomes wholly freed from all actions, as the lotus-leaf [is untouched] by the waters.
**76**
Eating this or that, clothed in whatever [comes to hand], tranquil, and lying down anywhere at all, the [sage who is the] Self of all beings is [thereby] released.
**77**
Though he perform [thousands of] horse-sacrifices, or [a hundred] thousand slayings of brahmins, the knower of {{paramārtha|supreme reality}}, [being] stainless, is touched neither by [their] merit nor by [their] sin. [Note: 'hayamedhasaharāṇy' is a scribal corruption, most likely for 'hayamedhasahasrāṇy', 'thousands of horse-sacrifices'.]

title: Paramārthasāra
text:
**78**
Free of intoxication, anger, elation, envy, despondency, fear, and harshness, his mind beyond speech, without praise-hymns or sacrificial calls (vaṣaṭ), the man of unfathomable understanding should wander about as though insentient (jaḍa).
**79**
Having thus apprehended the {{paramārtha|supreme reality}}, [which is] devoid of origination and destruction — his duty done, his birth made fruitful, [now] all-pervading — he abides as he pleases.
**80**
Who thus knows [the Self as] all-pervading, undivided, the Self of all, with [all] manifoldness shaken off, supreme bliss beyond compare — he becomes of that very substance.
**81**
Whether at a [sacred] ford or in the house of an outcaste (dog-cooker), [whether] even his memory be lost as he gives up the body, [the sage,] released [already] at the very moment of [his] knowledge, his grief slain, goes to {{kaivalya / kevalin|absolute aloneness/isolation}}.
**82**
[Resorting to] the service of a [sacred] ford [makes] for merit; dying in the dwelling of an outcaste [makes] for hell — but for one in whom there is no touch of the stain of merit or demerit, what is [any of] that to him?
**83**
As a man whose foot has slipped from the top of a tree falls to the ground though he does not wish it, so one who knows [the distinction of] the {{guṇa|qualities}}s and the {{puruṣa|conscious self}} becomes the Alone (kevalin — {{kaivalya / kevalin|the liberated one}}) even without wishing it.
**84**
Even one who, having begun the practice of the path to {{paramārtha|supreme reality}}, has not [yet] attained [the full state of] yoga — he too, indeed, [becomes] an enjoyer of the enjoyments of the world of the gods and, glad of mind, rejoices for a very long time.
**85**
As a king who is universal sovereign over [his] domains is honored by all people, so one who has fallen [short] of yoga is, throughout the worlds, honored by all the gods.
**86**
After a great length of time, the great one, [again] obtaining human birth and practicing yoga, attains the divine nectar [of immortality] — that which is the supreme abode of Viṣṇu. [Note: in the source TEI this verse carries xml:id="PAS_8", a duplicate-ID corruption; by reading order it is verse 86.]
**87**
Having surveyed the whole science of Vedānta, Śeṣa, [who is] the support of the world, composed this Essence of Supreme Truth in eighty-five {{āryā|the mora-counting metre of the whole poem}} [verses]. [Note: the colophon's count of 'eighty-five' (āryapañcāśītyā) does not match the 87 numbered verses transmitted; this is a known feature of the Ādiśeṣa recension and is left as transmitted.]
**colophon**
Thus the Paramārthasāra (Essence of Supreme Truth) is concluded.
